name: Booz Allen Hamilton Holding Corp
business: Sells AI, cyber, defense tech, data and digital modernization services and products mainly to US defense, intelligence and civil government agencies.

events.what: New EVP and CFO (first earnings call 2026-05-22, Q4 FY2026); predecessor Matthew Calderone resigned effective 2026-02-01, Kristine Martin Anderson interim
events.from: Sierra Space (SVP and CFO); earlier CFO of Boeing Defense, Space & Security; 12 years Stifel A&D equity analyst

events.what: COO adds President title; Shannon Fitzgerald to President of Civil; Richard Crowe to Chief Growth Officer (internal reshuffle)

Pending acquisition of Ultra I&C Mission Solutions (defense tech, edge compute, encryption products) for $720 million from Cobham Ultra (Advent); expected to close in fiscal Q2 (Jul to Sep 2026). CFO: strong double-digit growth, EBITDA margins well above 20%. Bolt-on, about 8.5% of market cap
events.who: Cobham Ultra Group / Ultra Mission Solutions

events.what: Acquisition of Defy Security (commercial cyber), about $324 million deployed in Q1 FY2027 for Defy plus venture investments

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Company guides adjusted EBITDA margin on revenue (including billable expenses), same basis as VA consensus EBITDA/revenue. The only numeric level is the one-year FY2027 guide of about 11% (fiscal year ending 2027-03-31), equal to FY2026's 11.0%, so it frames no expansion. Multi-year language (fixed price, outcome-based contracting, products, Ultra at well above 20% EBITDA margin) is qualitative with no year.

statements.quote: We expect to generate adjusted EBITDA in the range of $1.24 billion and $1.29 billion. This implies a full year adjusted EBITDA margin of about 11%.

statements.quote: Finally, from a margin perspective, we continue to expect approximately 11% margins for the year. This implies a step-down in margins for the rest of the year, particularly in 2Q, due to the end of some higher-margin civil programs and back-loaded investment spending.

statements.quote: Then, we've always said that margins are stronger on the fixed price work if we are allowed to deliver it in a way that it can add more value to the customer with more efficiency on our side.

statements.quote: I would say what we said is that really when it comes to revenue, we see strong double-digit growth. I think that that's going to continue for the next several years. EBITDA margins are well above the 20%.

street.gap_assumption: Baba labels are fiscal-year-end keyed and BAH names its fiscal year by the March end, so Baba FY2027 = company fiscal 2027 (ending 2026-03-31 is FY2026, actual). No multi-year target exists, so no gap is scored. Versus the one-year FY2027 guide of about 11%, consensus FY2027 at 11.16% sits about 16 bps ABOVE management (guide minus consensus = -16 bps). Street models flat margins (11.16% FY2027, 11.12% FY2028).

evidence_of_progress.note: Q4 FY2026 adj EBITDA margin 11.1%, +50 bps YoY; Q1 FY2027 11.9%, +130 bps YoY (Lahr, docs 197119 and 101215). Driven by contract execution, cost control, award fees and investment timing, while revenue fell 6.4% and 4.2%. Management guides a step-down for the rest of FY2027 to about 11% for the year.

verdict: Cheap and down 61% with a new external CFO and a pending $720M defense tech bolt-on, but the 11-year CEO frames only a flat one-year 11% margin guide that the street already models; D scores only on stabilized revisions.
open_questions: Will Lahr introduce a multi-year margin framework once Ultra closes and guidance is updated next quarter?
How much margin uplift can fixed-price and outcome-based contracting deliver, and on what timeline?
Does civil revenue stabilize in the second half, or does the 12-month -9.4% EBITDA revision resume?
